##Part A: Basic Operations

# A1 Create v as the sequence 5, 10, 15, ..., 50 using seq(). Print its length, sum and mean.
```{r}
v <- seq(5, 50, by = 5)
print(v)
print(length(v))
print(sum(v))
print(mean(v))
```
##A2 Create w that repeats the vector c(1, 2, 3) four times, and z that repeats each element of c(1, 2, 3) fourr times. Print both.

```{r}
w <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), times = 4)
z <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), each = 4)
print(w)
print(z)
```
## A3 Compute and print: remainder of 17 / 5, integer division of 17 %/% 5, 2^10, sqrt(144), and pi rounded to 3 decimals.
```{r}
print(17 %% 5)
print(17 %/% 5)
print(2^10)
print(sqrt(144))
print(round(pi, 3))
```
##A4 Givem a <- c(2,4,6) and b <-c( 1,3,5,7), print a+B, a * b, the logical comparison  a>b, and the dot product sum(a*b).
```{r}
a <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)
b <- c(1, 3, 5, 7)

print(a + b)
print(a * b)
print(a > b)

print(sum(a * b))
```
##A5 Use paste() to produce "Student-1" " Student-2" "Student-3". Then identify the datatype of 42, 42L, "42", 41i, and TRUE. What are  its outputs?

```{r}
class(42)
class(42L)
class("42")
class(41i)
class(TRUE)
```

###Part B; Dta Frames and Conditional Statements

##B1 Create a data frame students with 8 rows and these columns( use stringASFactors = FALSE; sex is "M" or "F")
```{r}
students <- data.frame (id = 1:8,
                        
                        name = c("Alice", "Bruno", "Chen", "Dana", "Elif", "Farid", "Grace", "Hiro"),
                        
                        sex = c("F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
                        
                        section = c("A", "B", "A", "C", "B", "C", "A", "B"),
                        
                        midterm = c(78, 85, 92, 67, 74, 88, 95, 59),
                        
                        final = c(82, 79, 96, 71, 80, 91, 93, 65),
                        
                        attendance = c(95, 88, 100, 72, 90, 85, 98, 60),
                        
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
print(students)
```


##B2 Display the sructure, dimensions, columns names, and summary of studnts.

```{r}
str(students)
dim(students)
colnames(students)
summary(students)
```

##B3 Add a column average = the mean of midterm and final for each student, rounded to 1 decimal
```{r}
students$average <- round((students$midterm + students$final) / 2, 1)

print(students)
```
##B4 Add a logical column passed that is TRUE when average >= 70 an attendance >=75.
```{r}
students$passed <- (students$average >= 70) & (students$attendance >= 75)

print(students)
```
##B5 using if else(), add a column standing with thses values based on average:

1. "Honors" if average >= 90
2. "Good" if average >= 75 (and below 90)
3. " Needs Support" otherwise

```{r}
students$standing <- ifelse(students$average >= 90, "Honors",
                            
                            ifelse(students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))

print(students)

```

##B6 Write a function classify(score) that uses if / else if/ else chain and returns " Distinction" for 85 or above, "Merit" for 70 to 84, "Pass" for 50 to 69, and "Fail" below 50. Test it with sapply(c(90,73,55,40), classify) and print the result.
```{r}
classify <- function(score) {
  if (score >= 85) {
    
    return("Distinction")
  } else if (score >= 70) {
    return("Merit")
  } else if (score >= 50) {
    return("Pass")
  } else {
    return("Fail")
  }
}

test_scores <- c(90, 73, 55, 40)

print(sapply(test_scores, classify))
```
###Part C: rbind() and cbind()

##C1 Create a data frame new_studnts with two studntes. Its columns must match the original, including, average, passed and standing, comuted the same way: 

1. id 9, Ines, F, section C, midterm 81, final 84, attendance 92
2. id 10, Jamal, M, section A, midterm 70, final 68, attendance 80

Use rbind() to append them to students, saving the result as student_all.

```{r}
new_students <- data.frame(
  
  id = c(9, 10),
  name = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
  sex = c("F", "M"),
  section = c("C", "A"),
  midterm = c(81, 70),
  final = c(84, 68),
  attendance = c(92, 80),
  average = c(82.5, 69.0),
  passed = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  standing = c("Good", "Needs Support"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

students_all <- rbind(students, new_students)
print(students_all)
```
##C2 Create quiz vector, attach via cbind(), and confirm class is data.frame.

```{r}
quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)
students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz)

class(students_all)
```

# C3 Create matrix m with midterm and final, use rbind() to add mean row.
```{r}
m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final)
mean_row <- colMeans(m)
m <- rbind(m, mean = mean_row)

print(m)
```

##C4 In a comment (2-3 sentences), explain what error rbind()
produces if the data frames have different column names, and show the output if you safely catch it with tryCatc()

tryCatch(rbind(students, bad), error = function(e) {message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e)) NULL}).

Answer: Because when data frames was used it needs to have the same match so that it will be successful code and never gonna be an error

###Part D: Subsetting

##D1 Extract the name column in three ways: $, [[...]], and [, ...].

```{r}
print(students_all$name)
print(students_all[["name"]])
print(students_all[, "name"])

```
##D2 Extract rows 2 to 5 and only the columns name, midterm, final.

```{r}
print(students_all[2:5, c("name", "midterm", "final")])
```
##D3 Using logical subsetting, select students with attendance above 90.

```{r}
print(students_all[students_all$attendance > 90, ])
```
##D4 Using subset(), select students of sex "F" in section "A" or "C" whose final >= 75; return only name, section and final.

```{r}
print(subset(students_all, sex == "F" & (section == "A" | section == "C") & final >= 75, select = c(name, section, final)))
```
###Part E: Basic Factors
##E1 Convert section and sex in students_all to factor(). Print levels()of each.
```{r}
students_all$section <- factor(students_all$section)
students_all$sex <- factor(students_all$sex)

levels(students_all$section)
levels(students_all$sex)
```

## E2 Use table() to count students per section and per section
*Try the two-way table of sex by section. table(students_all$sex, students_all$section). What is the output.

```{r}
table(students_all$sex)
table(students_all$section)
table(students_all$sex, students_all$section)
```

## E3 Print as.integer() of the sex factor. In a comment, explaint what the integers represent.
```{r}
as.integer(students_all$sex)

# Each integer is the position of the level: 1 = "F" (first level),
# 2 = "M" (second level). Levels are sorted alphabetically by default.
```

## E4 Create a new factor sex_label from sex using factor() with levels = c("F", "M") and labels = c("Female", "Male"). Add it to students_a;; and print its levels()
```{r}
students_all$sex_label <- factor(students_all$sex,
                                 levels = c("F", "M"),
                                 labels = c("Female", "Male"))

levels(students_all$sex_label)
```

## E5 Print summary() of sex_label. Then, using logical subsetting and mean(), print the mean average for each level of sex_label.

```{r}
 summary(students_all$sex_label)

sapply(levels(students_all$sex_label), function(lv) {
  mean(students_all$average[students_all$sex_label == lv])
})
```
